key_insight: Transfer learning plus a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász loss makes a lightweight BiSeNetV2 seam segmenter far more robust to harsh reflections without changing model size or speed.
engineering_relevance: This improves real-time weld seam perception for construction robots, helping automated welding stay accurate on thin, reflective, and illumination-challenged metallic joints.
method: Fine-tuned BiSeNetV2 with transfer learning for seam segmentation
Used a hybrid Cross-Entropy + Lovász objective to stabilize learning and improve overlap quality
Kept architecture, FLOPs, and inference speed unchanged while targeting reflection robustness
evidence_signal: The proposed method reached 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by 22.36 points over the OHEM baseline and recovering 96.33% of severe zero-IoU failure cases under reflective conditions.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown in the reported dataset and may depend on the quality and diversity of reflective welding scenes used during training and validation.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
